name: Zeeb
title: Midianite Prince Killed by Gideon's Men
summary: Zeeb was one of the two Midianite princes killed by the Ephraimites during Gideon's battle against the Midianites. Along with Oreb, he was pursued after Gideon inflicted a great defeat on the army of Midian. His name, which means 'wolf', has remained as a symbol of God's judgment upon Israel's enemies.

keyEvents.title: Gideon's Victory over the Midianites
keyEvents.description: Gideon defeated the large Midianite army with only 300 men, causing the Midianites to flee in panic. This was the prelude to the pursuit during which Zeeb was killed.

keyEvents.title: The Ephraimites Are Called to Battle
keyEvents.description: Gideon sent word to the Ephraimites to cut off the Midianites' escape at the fords of the Jordan, and they captured the two Midianite princes Oreb and Zeeb.

keyEvents.title: Zeeb Is Killed at the Winepress
keyEvents.description: Zeeb was killed at the winepress that later came to be named after him—the Winepress of Zeeb. The Ephraimites brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.

keyEvents.title: Gideon Calms the Discontent of the Ephraimites
keyEvents.description: After the killing of Zeeb and Oreb, the Ephraimites were angry with Gideon because they had not been called from the beginning. Gideon answered them diplomatically, pointing out that their capture of the princes was more important than all his own efforts.

keyEvents.title: The Memory of Zeeb's Fall in the Psalms
keyEvents.description: The psalmist asks God to treat Israel's enemies as He treated Midian and its princes Oreb and Zeeb, as a model of God's righteous judgment.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Prophecy about Midian's Defeat
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah refers to the defeat at the Rock of Zeeb as a picture of God's coming deliverance of His people from oppression.
